🔧 How to Implement Map

Option 1 (BEST):

Use:

  • react-simple-maps

Bash
npm install react-simple-maps

Example:

TypeScript
import { ComposableMap, Geographies, Geography } from "react-simple-maps";

export default function MapCard() {
  return (
    <div className="bg-[#111827] p-6 rounded-2xl">
      <h3 className="mb-4">Nigeria Overview</h3>

      <ComposableMap>
        <Geographies geography="/nigeria.json">
          {({ geographies }) =>
            geographies.map((geo) => (
              <Geography
                key={geo.rsmKey}
                geography={geo}
                fill="#1A2332"
                stroke="#0B1220"
              />
            ))
          }
        </Geographies>
      </ComposableMap>
    </div>
  );
}

💡 Recommendation:

  • Color states based on:

    • WAEC pass rate

    • JAMB performance

  • Add hover tooltip (very important)

ChatGPT said:

Yeah — what you’re seeing is the new Tailwind v4 + Next.js default setup. It’s different, but actually more powerful once you understand it.

Right now, your config is theme-based (CSS variables) instead of hardcoded Tailwind colors.

Let’s cleanly convert this into your dark dashboard system without breaking anything.

🧠 What You Currently Have (Important)

Your setup uses:

CSS
@import "tailwindcss";

👉 This means:

  • No tailwind.config.js needed (by default)

  • Theme is controlled via CSS variables

  • Tailwind classes like bg-background will map to your variables

🎯 Goal

Turn this:

CSS

Into your dashboard style:

CSS

✅ 1. Replace Your globals.css (Clean + Dashboard Ready)

Use this 👇

CSS
@import "tailwindcss";

/* 🌑 Core Theme */
:root {
  --background: #0B1220;
  --foreground: #E5E7EB;

  --card: #111827;
  --card-foreground: #F9FAFB;

  --primary: #3B82F6;
  --secondary: #06B6D4;

  --muted: #1A2332;
  --border: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05);
}

/* Optional: Remove light mode completely */
@media (prefers-color-scheme: light) {
  :root {
    --background: #0B1220;
    --foreground: #E5E7EB;
  }
}

/* Apply globally */
body {
  background: var(--background);
  color: var(--foreground);
  font-family: var(--font-sans, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif);
}

🎨 2. How to Use These in Your Components

Instead of hardcoding:

❌ BAD:

TypeScript
className="bg-[#111827]"

✅ GOOD:

TypeScript
className="bg-[var(--card)]"

Example:

TypeScript
<div className="bg-[var(--card)] text-[var(--card-foreground)] rounded-2xl p-6">

🔥 3. Create Reusable Utility Classes (VERY SMART)

Add this inside your CSS:

CSS
@layer components {
  .card {
    background: var(--card);
    color: var(--card-foreground);
    border-radius: 1rem;
    padding: 1.5rem;
    border: 1px solid var(--border);
  }

  .card-hover {
    transition: all 0.3s ease;
  }

  .card-hover:hover {
    transform: scale(1.02);
  }
}

Now you can just do:

TypeScript
<div className="card card-hover">

⚠️ 4. Important Mistake to Avoid

Don’t mix too much of this:

TypeScript
bg-blue-500 bg-[var(--card)]

👉 Pick ONE system:

  • either Tailwind colors

  • or your theme variables

👉 For dashboards → use variables (cleaner + scalable)

/app/layout.tsx

import type { Metadata } from "next";
import { Geist, Geist_Mono } from "next/font/google";
import "./globals.css";

const geistSans = Geist({
  variable: "--font-geist-sans",
  subsets: ["latin"],
});

const geistMono = Geist_Mono({
  variable: "--font-geist-mono",

🧩 STEP 5: Create Map Component

📌 /components/dashboard/MapCard.tsx

TypeScript
"use client";

import { ComposableMap, Geographies, Geography } from "react-simple-maps";

const data = {
  Lagos: 80,
  Kano: 60,
  Abuja: 75,
};

export default function MapCard() {
  return (
    <div className="bg-[var(--card)] border border-[var(--border)] rounded-2xl p-6">
      
      <h2 className="text-lg font-semibold mb-4">
        Nigeria Exam Overview
      </h2>

      <ComposableMap>
        <Geographies geography="/nigeria.json">
          {({ geographies }) =>
            geographies.map((geo) => {
              const state = geo.properties.NAME_1;
              const value = data[state] || 50;

              return (
                <Geography
                  key={geo.rsmKey}
                  geography={geo}
                  fill={`rgba(59,130,246, ${value / 100})`}
                  stroke="#0B1220"
                  style={{
                    default: { outline: "none" },
                    hover: { fill: "#06B6D4", outline: "none" },
                    pressed: { outline: "none" },
                  }}
                />
              );
            })
          }
        </Geographies>
      </ComposableMap>

    </div>
  );
}

Ahh — this is not your network.
This is a dependency conflict, and it’s very common with newer Next.js setups.

🧠 What’s Actually Happening

Error says:

Bash
react-simple-maps requires:
react ^16 || 17 || 18

But your project is likely using:

👉 React 19 (Next.js latest)

So npm is like:

“These versions don’t officially match 😤”

✅ 3 Ways to Fix It (Ranked Best → Worst)

🥇 OPTION 1 (BEST): Use --legacy-peer-deps

Run:

Bash
npm install react-simple-maps --legacy-peer-deps

👉 This tells npm:

“Install it anyway, I know what I’m doing.”

✔ Safe in this case
✔ Works for most modern setups

🥈 OPTION 2: Use --force

Bash
npm install react-simple-maps --force

👉 More aggressive version of above

⚠️ Use only if option 1 fails

🥉 OPTION 3 (Alternative Library — cleaner long-term)

If you want zero conflicts, use:

👉 react-svg-map OR d3

But:

  • more setup

  • less beginner friendly

🎯 My Recommendation (For YOU)

👉 Use this:

Bash
npm install react-simple-maps --legacy-peer-deps

Then continue — it will work fine.

⚠️ Important Note (Real-world advice)

Even though:

react-simple-maps doesn’t officially list React 19

👉 It still works perfectly in most cases.

This is just npm being strict.

🧱 STEP 1: Make Map a Client Component

📌 Create:

Bash
/components/dashboard/MapCard.tsx

🧩 Paste this:

TypeScript
"use client";

import { ComposableMap, Geographies, Geography } from "react-simple-maps";
import { useState } from "react";

const geoUrl = "/nigeria.json";

// Example data (you will replace later with real WAEC/JAMB data)
const data: Record<string, number> = {
  Lagos: 85,
  Kano: 60,
  FCT: 75,
  Rivers: 70,
};

export default function MapCard() {
  const [hovered, setHovered] = useState<string | null>(null);

  return (
    <div className="bg-[var(--card)] border border-[var(--border)] rounded-2xl p-6 h-[400px] relative">

      <h2 className="mb-4 text-lg font-semibold">
        Nigeria Exam Overview
      </h2>

      {/* Map */}
      <ComposableMap
        projection="geoMercator"
        style={{ width: "100%", height: "100%" }}
      >
        <Geographies geography={geoUrl}>
          {({ geographies }) =>
            geographies.map((geo) => {
              const state = geo.properties.NAME_1;
              const value = data[state] || 40;

              return (
                <Geography
                  key={geo.rsmKey}
                  geography={geo}
                  onMouseEnter={() => setHovered(state)}
                  onMouseLeave={() => setHovered(null)}
                  fill={`rgba(59,130,246, ${value / 100})`}
                  stroke="#0B1220"
                  style={{
                    default: { outline: "none" },
                    hover: {
                      fill: "#06B6D4",
                      outline: "none",
                    },
                    pressed: { outline: "none" },
                  }}
                />
              );
            })
          }
        </Geographies>
      </ComposableMap>

      {/* Tooltip */}
      {hovered && (
        <div className="absolute bottom-4 left-4 bg-black/70 text-white text-sm px-3 py-1 rounded-lg">
          {hovered} — {data[hovered] || 40}%
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
